title: I started building a news app while I was still in high school.
body:
It started with a simple frustration. I was tired of reading headlines that felt designed to make me angry or anxious. I wanted to know what was happening in the world without having to wade through clickbait or endless doomscrolling.

My friends and I were constantly sharing links, but we rarely had time to actually read the articles. We needed a way to get the facts quickly and personally. That gap is what led to Headlinne.

Building this as a teenager taught me that news isn't just about information. It is about relevance. The internet is flooded with content, but it is starving for context. We built an AI that doesn't just aggregate links but actually understands what you care about so you can spend less time searching and more time understanding.

It is not about replacing human editors or journalism. It is about using technology to make sure the right information finds the right person at the right time.
cta: You can see how we are rethinking the daily news cycle at HEADLINNE.com.
